name: as-written-plus
note: The annual sequence EXACTLY as written -- the omnibill every year, decay every year -- with the one change that makes it work: the push table raised +2 to 2/3/4. Measured against the shipped baseline it realigns 13.8 states a game against 5.8, pins nothing at the cap against 3.5, and passes 7.3 bills against 3.1. Biennial decay was never the fix; it was a workaround for a push table too small to outrun an annual -2, and it costs half the legislative layer and saturates the map. See findings/decay-push-tradeoff.ts.

placeholders.primaryGeneral.extremistPrimary: Extremism is a primary bonus and a general penalty, and no magnitude was ever printed.
placeholders.primaryGeneral.crossBenchPrimaryPenalty: Cross-benching is a primary penalty, and no magnitude was printed.
placeholders.lean.decayFrequency: Open question 1 -- SETTLED 2026-08-31 by arithmetic, not simulation. Annual decay is -2 per cycle against a maximum push of +2, so sustained blowouts net zero and lean pins at 2 forever: realignment is impossible. Biennial (-1) against margin-based pushes accumulates. See engine/rules/lean.test.ts and findings/decay-push-tradeoff.ts.
placeholders.lean.governorPushes: Open question; 'never' falls out of the priority rule, 'with-lean' is the alternative under test.
placeholders.lean.maxLean: No cap is stated. Without one, lean is unbounded.
placeholders.draft.districtsPerPack: Wired into defaultPick's draft heuristic in place of a hardcoded default -- see the comment above defaultPick in engine/game.ts. Swept end-to-end and district holdings per player come out flat regardless of its value; something else sets map fill rate, not this field. See sim/scratch-district-threshold-ablation.ts.
placeholders.game.victory: Open question -- STILL OPEN, and now with evidence that none of the four original candidates works. Term-based conditions (two/three terms) terminate tightly but concentrate all value in one race: the SAME agent pool goes from 28% to 90% purely by switching points -> three-terms. Bills-passed keeps the field balanced (top 33%) but leaves 37-42% of games unfinished and runs to a median 34-49 years. Shipping points + a year cap as the least-bad playable default. See hf7y/american-cycle#13, still open.
placeholders.economy.*: The economy is described as a shape (random walk with memory, 2d6 roll-under on accumulated G) but prints no bounds or step sizes.
placeholders.legislature.reactionGoodOnRollAtLeast: A reaction is rolled immediately on passage, and nothing says on what.
placeholders.game.deckOutEnds: Deck-out was named as the ending, but also has defeated politicians circulate back through the draft. Circulation wins: talon+discard GROW from 79 to 273 cards over a hundred years, so deck-out is unreachable and cannot be the backstop it was treated as.
placeholders.lean.uncontestedPush: A push scales with how decisively a race was won, and nothing says what a walkover does -- a race nobody contested has no margin at all. 0 leaves the map a driftless random walk and the central thesis unimplemented; 1 produces genuine realignment. Two measurements against real district returns disagree: sim/scratch-uncontested-predicts-movement.ts found no persistence signal at the effective-competitiveness threshold; sim/uncontested-predictiveness.ts, a differently-designed replication, found a significant positive multi-cycle effect under the strict unopposed definition. See hf7y/american-cycle#10. See hf7y/american-cycle#51.
placeholders.primaryGeneral.billCounterPips: A good reaction rewards yes-voters and a bad one penalises them at the next election, in both rounds, and that the card's accumulated counters are read off at resolution -- but prints no magnitude. One pip a counter is a stand-in.
placeholders.lean.pushByMargin: The printed push table is 0/1/2. Raised to 2/3/4 here, which is what lets the literal annual decay work: an annual -2 needs a push that can outrun it. Not a deviation so much as the number the annual sequence itself requires.
placeholders.resolution.incumbencyPrimary: Incumbency was called "a calibration check on +1", but a primary is 2d6 vs 2d6 (SD 3.42) against a general's 3d6 (SD 4.18), so one scalar cannot serve both rounds. 4 puts contested primary incumbent survival at 87.2% (was 91.2% under the 1d6 candidate die hf7y/american-cycle#94 replaced -- this value is NOT recalibrated to the new die, see hf7y/american-cycle#20). NOTE the benchmark population: the ~98% renomination rate quoted for real House incumbents is over ALL primaries including unopposed ones, so it is not the matching figure. Real CONTESTED survival is unverified.
placeholders.resolution.crossOfficeIncumbency: The stepping stone to higher office, flat. One number for every pair of offices: the primary/general asymmetry a table would encode is already emergent from the board, and the history refutes it (sitting House members won 61% of Senate primaries and 63% of the generals).
placeholders.primaryGeneral.crossBenchCap: The accumulated counters are simply read off, and uncapped they read ~30. But cross-benching is also structurally necessary to pass anything at a 60% Senate threshold, so an uncapped record makes cooperation career-ending. 3 puts the mean at 2.35 pips, 0.97 of the primary's 2.42 SD.
placeholders.scoring: v0.2 item 1. Weights for the EPILOGUE, not a running tally: score is a pure function of the board, so it can fall. Office weights are v0.1's win awards, re-read as what a seat is worth while it is HELD.
placeholders.scoring.cardInHand: Unprinted: the build doc lists cards in hand as scoring but not the weight. Worried this could dilute the epilogue, since base hand size is large -- measured instead of assumed (sim/scratch-cardinhand-share.ts): candidates actually held at scoring time, net of districts and cards already played, make this a small share of a final score, nowhere near what the raw hand-size arithmetic suggested. Kept at the shipped weight.
placeholders.amendment: v0.2 item 3. Article V's fractions are not tuning knobs -- two-thirds to call and three-quarters to ratify are what make thirteen states a blocking minority, which is the anti-runaway claim. `dice`, `target` and `rescindTarget` ARE tuning and are unprinted anywhere, so they are fitted to the postwar ratification rate instead (5 of 7 amendments sent to the states after 1947 were ratified; 27 of 33 all-time). tracks/d.ts D6 grades that fit. `windowYears` is INERT above about 5: rescission is a one-time act, so every state is decided within a few years and a longer window changes nothing -- 8 and 12 give identical results to three decimals. Rescission's SHAPE is invented too, not only its target: one-shot per state -- a rescinded state stays out rather than being re-litigated every year -- and gated on the challenger holding standing there (the governorship, a matching district, or the lean) rather than open to anyone. See the WHERE/WHEN comment on ratify() in engine/game.ts.
placeholders.primaryGeneral.partyFitPips: v0.2 item 5, unprinted. What it costs to run under a label whose current officeholders you do not resemble -- Thurmond's 1964 switch, priced.
placeholders.primaryGeneral.offDistrictPips: v0.2 item 6, unprinted. The price of a yes-vote on a bill your districts do not want.
placeholders.primaryGeneral.bruisingPrimaryMargin: Unprinted margin, in pips, below which a primary win still counts as a bruising showing rather than a clean one -- the McCarthy give-in case in HISTORICAL-CASES.md.
placeholders.primaryGeneral.bruisingPrimaryPips: Unprinted penalty a bruising primary win carries into the general, the same shape as the other primary-into-general counters here.
placeholders.legislature.impeachBackfirePips: v0.2 item 7, flat. The 1998 midterm preceded the Senate vote by three months, so the penalty attaches to the attempt and there is no conviction margin to scale by. Scaling by strain is v0.3.
placeholders.legislature.shutdownPips: v0.2 item 8. Weighted toward the party perceived as making the demand, NOT toward incumbents: 1995-96, 2013 and 2018-19 all point the same way and in two of the three the blamed party held the majority.
placeholders.legislature.billLeanPips: A passed bill's tags now write to the map too, a flat push toward the majority party in every district on the table they touch, mirroring the shutdown and impeachment-backfire pips already here. Unprinted anywhere; set level with those flat pushes rather than swept.
placeholders.economy.shockOnRollAtMost: v0.2 item 9, the CHEAP version on purpose. If it moves the determination point the positional version is never built; if it does not, the complexity has been earned.
placeholders.hand.bonusPresident: Office hand-size bonuses were printed without saying per-seat or per-office. Read per seat rather than per office they compound into a runaway as seats accumulate; findings/runaway-no-brake.ts measures the determination point with them switched off. Implemented per office held, same as hand.bonusSenator, hand.bonusGovernor and hand.bonusRepresentative.
placeholders.hand.bonusSenator: Per office held, not per seat -- see hand.bonusPresident.
placeholders.hand.bonusGovernor: Per office held, not per seat -- see hand.bonusPresident.
placeholders.hand.bonusRepresentative: Per office held, not per seat -- see hand.bonusPresident.
